title: Viruses: Structure and Replication
text: Viruses are microscopic infectious agents that can only replicate inside living cells of organisms. They consist of genetic material (DNA or RNA) enclosed in a protein coat called a capsid, and sometimes surrounded by a lipid membrane called an envelope. Viruses infect all types of life forms, from animals and plants to bacteria and archaea. The viral life cycle involves attachment to a host cell, injection of genetic material, replication using host cellular machinery, assembly of new virus particles, and release. Viruses cause many human diseases including influenza, HIV/AIDS, hepatitis, and COVID-19. Unlike bacteria, viruses cannot be treated with antibiotics.
